quote: So Zoe Zoe Pitts is the one who owns the house.
stewart_read: Jacob discloses that Zoe, his fiancée, is the actual owner on title while he is merely on the deed — this is a co-owner disclosure that should trigger inclusion of Zoe on any future appointment, per the spouse/co-owner protocol.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be planning to loop Zoe in once an appointment is actually scheduled, since no appointment was set on this call at all.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly note that Zoe must be present for any consultant call, especially since the credit qualifier that follows is run against her, not Jacob.

quote: It will guarantee savings within the first year you guys have solar. Just as long as you have well, sorry. As long as Zoe has a credit score above 670, then you guys will qualify. Is that the case for you guys?
stewart_read: The rep runs the hard credit qualifier against Zoe — the actual title-owner and correct financial subject — but accepts the answer secondhand through Jacob ('Yeah.') without ever getting Zoe on the line or flagging that her stated score needs confirmation from her directly.
alternative_hypothesis: Jacob may know Zoe's credit standing with confidence and this could be treated as reliable proxy information for a setter-stage call.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager: proxy-confirmed credit answers on the actual decision-maker are a qualifier-integrity gap — the closer needs to know this number was never confirmed by Zoe herself, and Zoe was never brought into the conversation at all despite being the title-holder.

quote: Yeah. We're we're also a fully in house company, which makes it nice because we don't go through any third parties or anything.
stewart_read: This is a borderline case, not a clean violation — the rep is responding directly to a differentiator (in-house, ability to move panels) that Jacob himself raised as his stated reason for taking the call, so the explanation is reactive to customer-initiated curiosity rather than unprompted feature-selling.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter reading would still classify this as scope creep since panel-lift/reroof mechanics are closer-tier detail regardless of who raised the topic first.
coaching_implication: Not a priority coaching item — the rep is answering the customer's own question briefly and moves on immediately after; contrast with SESSION10 where the rep argued technical points unprompted and at length.

quote: which I thought was pretty unique and worth at least a conversation
stewart_read: Jacob explicitly frames himself as already curious and willing to engage — a strong forward-leaning signal on a warm referral lead that the rep could have anchored into a firm appointment ask immediately after.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to strike while this door is open — this is the exact moment to pivot into locking a specific day/time for the consultant call, not to keep gathering info and let the call trail off.

quote: Oh, actually, the last thing I need from you is just a copy of your kilowatt usage on your AEP bill.
stewart_read: The rep treats bill collection as the final action item and then ends the call without ever proposing an appointment day/time — the entire call produces no scheduled next step beyond 'send the bill when you get home.'
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may intend to set the appointment on a follow-up call once the bill is received, treating this as a two-touch process by design.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always lock a tentative appointment slot on the same call, even if it's contingent on the bill arriving — 'let's plan for Thursday at 4, and I'll confirm once I have your usage numbers' — rather than leaving the appointment entirely open.

quote: Yeah. That would be amazing. I'll just send you a text then, and then you can just send that whenever you get home.
stewart_read: The rep had an engaged, referral-warm customer and a concrete bill range ($200-400) in hand but closed the call with a purely administrative texting logistics line instead of using the bill pain or Zoe's involvement to pull the customer toward a firm booked appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally keeping the call short since Jacob was driving, deferring the harder close to a follow-up text/call once safer to talk.
coaching_implication: Review whether ending calls with only a bill-photo promise and no appointment is a broader pattern for this rep — each call should end with a locked next step, not just a data-collection promise.
